title: Buildertrend alternatives: what bidding tools cost instead
description: Buildertrend estimating and bid requests are reported to start at its middle plan. Six alternatives priced by headcount or with takeoff in every plan, with real prices.
lead: Buildertrend's estimating and bid requests are reported to start at the middle plan, so the real entry price for bidding is higher than the headline. Here is what the alternatives charge.
why: Third-party sources report that the estimating suite, takeoff and bid requests start at the Advanced plan, at $499 per month billed annually or $799 on monthly billing. Sources disagree on the figures and the vendor pricing page could not be retrieved when checked.
All Buildertrend plans include unlimited users, and onboarding is reported at $500 to $2,000 extra in the first year.
The alternatives fall into two groups: tools priced by headcount instead of by tier, and estimating-first tools that put takeoff in every plan.

picks.pickIf: You want all features without tiers: $199 a month with one user, then $20 per extra internal user.
picks.watchOut: Headcount pricing adds up in a large office. See the head-to-head with Buildertrend.

picks.pickIf: You want bid comparison in the starting plan, from $49 a month billed annually.
picks.watchOut: Basic covers one user. Most teams need Standard ($105, three users) or Plus ($166, eight users).

picks.pickIf: You are a residential builder who wants takeoff and estimating in every plan.
picks.watchOut: Pricing is third-party reported ($199 to $599 a month) because the vendor page could not be retrieved.

picks.pickIf: Client-facing proposals, CRM and lead generation matter more to you than commercial bidding.
picks.watchOut: Reported prices vary widely by source ($65 to $499 a month), and extra users are reported at $60 a month.

picks.pickIf: You are a specialty subcontractor who bills fixed-price and AIA jobs.
picks.watchOut: Cost-plus and time-and-materials contracts start at Advanced ($329 to $399 a month).

picks.pickIf: You want AI-generated estimates from photos, blueprints or site visits.
picks.watchOut: It is built for residential work and pricing is not published. A 7-day trial is offered.

verdict: If the price of getting bidding tools in Buildertrend is the issue, JobTread and Contractor Foreman are the closest direct comparisons with published prices.
If your office is large, compare per-user pricing carefully, because Buildertrend does not charge per user.
If you are mostly a subcontractor, Knowify or a bid network may fit better than a tool built for home builders.
